config.title: Zustand for Global State

intro.title: Zustand for Global State
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that uses Zustand, a lightweight state management library, to manage global state. You'll learn how to create a Zustand store to hold and update shared data across components. The core concept is global state management, which allows different parts of your app to access and modify the same data without passing it through multiple layers. You'll work with TypeScript for type safety and Angular components to display and interact with the state. By the end, you'll have a functional app that demonstrates how Zustand simplifies state handling in Angular projects.
intro.usecase: In real applications, Zustand provides a lightweight solution for managing shared state across multiple components. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce dashboards where product filters, cart items, and user preferences need to be synchronized across different views without prop drilling. It's commonly used in admin panels where sidebar collapse state, theme preferences, and notification settings must persist globally. Developers choose Zustand over Angular services when they need a simpler, more flexible state management solution that works consistently across complex component hierarchies.

objectives: Initialize a Zustand store within an Angular service to manage global application state
Configure store actions that manipulate state in response to user interactions
Integrate the Zustand store with Angular components using dependency injection
Bind component properties to store state to enable reactive UI updates
Apply store selectors to compute derived state from the global store
Control state updates by dispatching actions from component event handlers
Construct a complete state management solution using Zustand patterns in Angular

steps.title: Install Zustand and create a store interface
steps.instruction: Install Zustand via npm and create a TypeScript interface for the global store state. First, run the npm install command in your terminal,
steps.hint: Use npm install zustand to install the package. Then create a new TypeScript file (e.g., store.interface.ts) and define an interface with properties for your global state.

seedCode.App.tsx:
// Install Zustand: npm install zustand
// Then create a TypeScript interface for your global store state

steps.expectedOutcome: Zustand is installed as a dependency and a TypeScript interface is created to define the shape of your global state.
successCriteria: Zustand package is installed via npm and a TypeScript interface is defined with properties for the global store state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but ensure both actions are completed: install Zustand via npm and define a TypeScript interface for the store state.
steps.feedbackWrong: First, install Zustand using npm install zustand. Then, create a TypeScript interface to define your global store state properties.

steps.title: Create a Zustand store service
steps.instruction: Create an Angular service file named 'store.service.ts' that initializes a Zustand store using the interface you defined.
steps.hint: Generate a service using Angular CLI or manually create the file. Import create from 'zustand' and define your store with initial state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A service file is created with a Zustand store instance that can be injected into Angular components.
successCriteria: The service file exists with proper imports, uses create from 'zustand', and defines a store with initial state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a service file, but make sure it properly imports 'create' from 'zustand' and defines a store with initial state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service file is missing or doesn't properly initialize a Zustand store. Check that you're using 'create' from 'zustand' and defining the store correctly.

steps.title: Define store state and actions
steps.instruction: Inside your store service, add an initial state property called 'count' with a value of 0 and an action method called 'increment' that increases the count by 1.
steps.hint: In the Zustand store configuration, define a state object with a 'count' property and an 'increment' method that updates the state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store service now has an initial state with a count property and an increment action method.
successCriteria: The store service contains a 'count' property initialized to 0 and an 'increment' action method that updates the count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the 'count' property and the 'increment' method that updates it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the 'count' property with value 0 and an 'increment' method that increases the count by 1.

steps.title: Create a component to display store state
steps.instruction: Generate a new Angular component named 'DisplayStoreState' that will display values from the Zustand store. Use the Angular CLI command or manually create the component files.
steps.hint: You can use the Angular CLI: 'ng generate component DisplayStoreState' or manually create the component files (display-store-state.component.ts, display-store-state.component.html, display-store-state.component.css).
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Angular component named 'DisplayStoreState' is created with the basic component structure.
successCriteria: The component is named 'DisplayStoreState' and has the basic Angular component decorator and class structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it's named 'DisplayStoreState' and has the proper Angular component structure with @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to create an Angular component named 'DisplayStoreState' with the proper component structure.

steps.title: Inject the store service into the component
steps.instruction: In your DisplayStoreState component, inject the Zustand store service by adding a constructor parameter with the type of the store interface.
steps.hint: Use Angular's dependency injection: add a constructor parameter that receives the store service instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: injecting a service
constructor(private storeService: StoreService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the Zustand store service through dependency injection.
successCriteria: The DisplayStoreState component has a constructor that injects the store service with proper typing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the constructor parameter is properly typed with the store interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required constructor injection. Review how to inject services in Angular components.

steps.title: Subscribe to store state in the component
steps.instruction: In the DisplayStoreState component, implement the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to subscribe to the store state and the ngOnDestroy hook to clean up the subscription.
steps.hint: Use the store service's subscribe method to listen for state changes and store the subscription in a property for cleanup.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will properly subscribe to the store state changes and clean up the subscription when destroyed.
successCriteria: The DisplayStoreState component implements both ngOnInit and ngOnDestroy hooks with proper subscription handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've implemented one of the hooks, but remember to implement both ngOnInit for subscription and ngOnDestroy for cleanup.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have proper subscription lifecycle hooks. Make sure to implement both ngOnInit and ngOnDestroy.

steps.title: Display store state in the template
steps.instruction: In the DisplayStoreState component's template, add an interpolation binding to display the current store state values from the component's store property.
steps.hint: Use Angular's interpolation syntax {{ }} to bind the store state values from your component's store property in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will display the current store state values using interpolation bindings.
successCriteria: The DisplayStoreState component template contains interpolation bindings {{ store.propertyName }} to display store state values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct interpolation syntax {{ }} and accessing the store properties correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display store state values. Remember to use interpolation syntax {{ store.propertyName }} in the template.

steps.title: Create a second component to demonstrate global state
steps.instruction: Create another Angular component named 'SecondComponent' that also injects and displays the same Zustand store state.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define a new component class with its own template. Inject the store service using inject(useStore).
steps.expectedOutcome: A second component is created that can access the same global Zustand store, demonstrating how multiple components share state.
successCriteria: A component named 'SecondComponent' is defined with @Component decorator and injects the useStore service.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it's properly defined with @Component decorator and injects the useStore service.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined. Remember to use @Component decorator with a selector and template, and inject the useStore service.

steps.title: Test the global state behavior
steps.instruction: Run the application and verify that clicking the buttons in one component updates the displayed state in both components simultaneously.
steps.hint: Start your development server and open the app in a browser. Click the increment and decrement buttons in either component and observe if both components show the same updated count.
steps.analogousExample:
// Testing global state behavior
// After running the app, click buttons and verify both components update
steps.expectedOutcome: The application runs successfully, and clicking buttons in either component updates the count display in both components, demonstrating shared global state.
successCriteria: The application runs without errors, and state changes in one component are reflected in both components simultaneously.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The application runs, but you might need to check if both components are properly subscribed to the store. Make sure both components are using the same store instance and that their templates display the store.count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The application doesn't run or the state isn't shared between components. Check that both components are properly injected with the same store service and that the store actions are correctly defined.
